answers.explanation: The passage says no young Emopa attracts a girl's admiration until he has killed a dangerous animal, so the young men hunt elephants for that reason.
The passage says many famous hunters had tried in the past without success to kill the lions, which confirmed the legend.
The lions played baw to decide whether the omens were good enough to raid a village or to wait.
The passage says many famous hunters had failed owing to lack of time.
Boldness and retreating into undergrowth are not superstitious reasons, so B is the one NOT superstitious.
The passage says immature adults can behave self-centredly, knowing what is right and choosing not to do it, which is deliberately irrational.
The passage describes the child as not yet having the developed concept of time that an adult has, so the difference is developmental.
The parent gives commands for the child's safety because the adult understands the consequences of actions better than the child.
At two the child knows he is a self and does not have to obey, so he refuses orders to assert his independence.
At two the child is aware that he is a self and separate from his mother.
A dismal picture is a gloomy, sad situation.
The passage says girls' education is not seen as equal in importance to boys', so girls are kept at home.
The non-literate woman is chained to the household by the need to gather fuel, prepare food and tend children.
Too late means she goes on producing children after she should have stopped.
The writer stresses that girls need equal educational opportunities with boys.
The passage is about codes and how they relate to education.
Restricted and elaborated codes are contrasting forms of language, so they are antonyms.
The passage describes two codes, the restricted and the elaborated.
The school does not speak to the child in the way he is spoken to at home, which creates discontinuity.
The passage says it is hard to tell what in an enormous output will prove saleable, which makes books different from other goods.
The selection problem is determining what will prove saleable and sell fast.
The passage offers three ways out: becoming a passive sales representative, selling safe items, and speculating on new publications.
Each of the proposed solutions is shown to have a serious drawback, so none is positive.
The story of the book given to the general shows that a book means something only to those for whom it has meaning.
To investigate is to look into something, so its opposite is to forget about it.
Agitated means upset, so its opposite is calm.
Obstacles are hindrances, so their opposite is advantages.
To sob is to cry, so its opposite is to laugh.
Ignoble means dishonourable, so its opposite is honourable.
Convalescing means recovering, so its opposite is deteriorating.
Boundless means without limit, so its opposite is limited.
To decry is to condemn, so its opposite is to extol.
An intrepid fighter is fearless, so the opposite is timid.
Imperceptible means not noticeable, so the opposite is obvious.
Antipathy is dislike, so its opposite is receptiveness.
To let sleeping dogs lie means not to stir up trouble.
Cold comfort means inadequate comfort.
To make good a promise means to fulfil it.
A smoke-screen is something that hides activities, which is closest to camouflage.
Up in the air means uncertain.
A hardline stand is an uncompromising one.
For want of evidence means for lack of proof.
Indomitable means unconquerable.
Restive means restless, which is closest to fidgety.
To underscore a point is to emphasize it.
Invaluable means priceless.
Potential resources are latent resources.
Aberrant means abnormal.
To be arraigned before a court is to be brought before it.
To speak candidly is to speak frankly.
A cheerful disposition is shown by a happy look.
Fortified means enriched.
Unsavoury details are unpleasant ones.
A precursor is a forerunner.
Such insignificant matters is the correct adjective.
To conceive of something is to imagine it, which fits a man walking on the moon.
Consist of is the verb needed here, so consist is correct as a verb followed by questions.
Animals in captivity are kept in confinement.
The team reached the summit of the mountain.
Laid is the past tense of lay, which takes an object such as the bed.
Knowledge is singular, so is tested is correct.
The buildings included schools, hospitals and private houses.
The time you returned tomorrow uses the simple past in a time clause.
The reported form of shall be able is should be able.
Had better is the correct modal form.
Had not heard fits the unreal conditional past.
The comic which she had been reading is the correct relative clause.
Was sick fits the completed period of last month.
Who is is the correct relative pronoun for a person, in the present.
Every one of his constituents knows, with a singular subject.
The correct spelling is privilege.
Lay bare your hearts means to reveal them.
To be used to eating bread without butter is the correct construction.
Greeted each other is the correct reciprocal form.
One can no longer, can one, with matching pronouns.
Oblivious to means unaware of, which fits the shift of attention.
There was no one to help him is the correct structure.
Cannot be true with cannot driving describes a present impossibility.
Had fainted is the past perfect, and started to run is the correct infinitive form.
Disposed to teaching is the correct gerund, with the tag are they.
It did not rain, so we would not have had to postpone the concert.
In all probability is the correct phrase.
An objection to something takes to.
To prohibit something from being brought takes from.
Discussed by the students is the correct passive construction.
To depend on someone takes on.
The point of the story is the correct phrase.
To be at pains means to take trouble.
To break down means to lose control emotionally.

Be that as it may is the correct idiom.
To make a plea for mitigation is the correct phrase before sentence.
To settle for means to accept less than desired.

Adjectives follow the order of opinion, size, then nationality, so smart little Japanese.
Two young, but highly competent, Nigerian accountants uses the correct order.
Shall we? is the correct tag after Let's.
To turn to someone for help is the correct verb.
